title: Olivia and the Painted Sky
subtitle: Air is a quiet prism
author: Olivia's Shelf
blurb: Olivia wonders why the sky is blue and the sunset red, and learns that air spills the Sun's blue light all over the day.

magic.launch: The little rocket pushed the air, and the air pushed back.
magic.drop: Everything falls. That pull has a name: gravity.

openai.instructions: Warm, clear storyteller reading a science picture book to a child. Curious, never lecturing. Pause at full stops.

pages.heading: A blue lid
pages.text: {Olivia} looked out. The sky was {blue}. The Sun was white-gold. "{Elon:elon/look}," she said. "Who painted that?"

pages.heading: A bundle of colors
pages.text: "Sunlight is a {bundle} of colors," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "Like the rainbow hiding in white light."

pages.heading: Blue spills first
pages.text: "Air is full of tiny bits," said Elon. "{Blue} light bounces off them more than red. Blue {spills} all over the sky."

pages.heading: That spilled light
pages.text: "The blue we see is spilled {sunlight}," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "The air is a quiet prism."

pages.heading: Why sunsets blush
pages.text: "At sunset the light travels {farther}," said Elon. "Blue is spilled away. {Red} and orange stay in the path."

pages.heading: Keep asking why
pages.text: "Why is space black?" asked {Olivia:olivia/ask}. "Almost no air to bounce the blue {around}," said {Elon:elon/teach}.

end.heading: The End
end.text: Sunlight hides a rainbow. Air spills the blue across the day. Evening keeps the red.
end.prompt: What color would you watch the sky wear tomorrow?

credits: Painted for Olivia's Shelf. Elon is a picture-book inventor who teaches physics; this is not a biography.

questions.right: Yes! White sunlight hides a rainbow.
questions.wrong: Elon said sunlight is a bundle of colors.

options.label: air spills blue light all over

questions.right: That's right. Tiny bits in the air bounce blue light around.
questions.wrong: Blue light bounces off the air more than red.

options.label: blue has spilled away on the long path

questions.right: Yes. The long path through air leaves red and orange.
questions.wrong: At sunset the light travels farther, so blue is spilled away.
